question.problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=2x(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=4y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Interpret the stability of the $x$-axis, the $y$-axis, and the equilibrium point (the origin) for the given decoupled system of linear differential equations.
question.worked_solution:
Writing our system in matrix form, we have
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/73afc7cad8d4018e66ce31d26275c6d3238e0b50bfc85c65c84abb3d1d9c3c3c.svg)
where ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/375392fe3e7223efb30963c4f51b76a08f868bdde210574bb8fb0f2e53f925be.svg)

Recall that a homogeneous system of linear differential equations has a single equilibrium (fixed point) at the origin.

Since our system is decoupled, its eigenvectors are the following:

- Eigenvalue $\lambda_1=2$ with the eigenvector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/b8dce83f78184c194c43b2cf2b4148549a4ff0504a0f663f6a338a8cca6dec2f.svg) The corresponding straight-line solutions of the form
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/796f9e0b1c5698e87439547b5c84e00d492a6c7893cfd6adb793bd0639147d25.svg)
lie on the $x$-axis and move away from the origin as $t \to \infty.$ So, the $x$-axis is the $\bbox[4pt, border: solid 1pt gainsboro]{\text{unstable}}$ line.

- Eigenvalue $\lambda_2=4$ with the eigenvector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/f9da7bff2e0d90f112ce26291e3c1074e766e141bdae4198870d49136ed6706a.svg) The corresponding straight-line solutions of the form
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/9d8a16728992f0ce055be81c84ae0e905417e2ed74c4e659b277ab7f4226e90a.svg)
lie on the $y$-axis and also move away from the origin as $t \to \infty.$ So, the $y$-axis is the $\bbox[4pt, border: solid 1pt gainsboro]{\text{unstable}}$ line.

Therefore, the equilibrium point (origin) is $\bbox[4pt, border: solid 1pt gainsboro]{\text{an unstable node (source)}}.$ 

**Note:** The phase portrait of the system looks as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/2b79201d15fe5d2a9896cdee09c0474b97bb933d75fcf478c6fdb37cb4d16742.png)
